about: What a Claude Code cloud session gets of the toolbox projects/felix/stack.tsv declares, and why.

Read by .claude/cloud/provision. Every plugin and skill row in stack.tsv needs an entry here, and the gate's cloud check fails when one is missing, so a new stack row forces a decision about the cloud instead of silently not arriving there.

Plugins never load in a cloud session, whether a user or a repository enables them (code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments, 'What carries over'). What does load is this repository's .claude/skills, .claude/agents and .claude/commands, so fetch entries are carried as those: provision downloads the plugin at the sha pinned here and copies its skills, agents and commands into the clone.

The shas are the ones installed on the founder's machine (~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json): 2026-09-25 for the official ones, 2026-10-12 for the five from the plugin directory, each at the commit the directory reviewed. So the cloud runs what a local session runs. Move a pin when the local install moves.

carry: fetch = downloaded at sha and copied into .claude/; builtin = Claude Code itself ships an equivalent under the same name; claude.ai = arrives through the skills enabled on claude.ai; no = not carried, and the note says why.
JSON rather than a .tsv because the engine never reads it: engine/harness/templates/schemas.tsv registers the tables the engine reads.
